In this review, we summarized the TCM dialectical approach to PCOS, its underlying mechanisms with TCM interventions, and some emerging therapeutic concepts, which are related to multiple signaling pathways. Briefly, TCM can improve PCOS by regulating the hypothalamus-pituitary-ovarian (HPO) axis, improving insulin sensitivity, and exerting anti-inflammatory and anti-oxidative effects, which are related to multiple signaling pathways. In addition, some studies have also suggested that TCM can promote the repair of the ovarian microenvironment and affect related cell signal transduction and proteins to improve PCOS. In summary, this review aims to provide theoretical support and new treatment perspectives for the clinical treatment strategies of PCOS.

title: Discovery of Q-Markers in traditional Chinese medicine based on machine learning: Application and verification in Xiaoyao Heji
abstract: Objective: Identification of quality marker (Q-Marker) is central to the modernization and quality control of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM). Existing methods, though diverse, lack a unified and scalable strategy to address the chemical and pharmacological complexity of TCM prescriptions. This study established a machine learning-driven framework to integrate multi-source data and systematically prioritize Q-Marker, using Xiaoyao Heji (XYHJ), a modern antidepressant formulation derived from Xiaoyao San, as a case study. Methods: Firstly, a dataset of 302 compounds was constructed by summarizing 14 reported Q-Marker discovery strategies and annotated with five core dimensions-compatibility, specificity, measurability, traceability, and effectiveness. Subsequently, five ranking models (RankNet, Random Forest, XGBoost, Linear Regression and K-Nearest Neighbors) were trained with 8-fold GroupKFold cross-validation and evaluated by normalized discounted cumulative gain (NDCG), mean average precision (MAP), and Recall. Thirdly, the optimal model was applied to XYHJ, followed by systematic characterization of chemical profiles, quantitative analysis, drug metabolism and pharmacokinetics (DMPK), quality transitivity, and bioactivity. Finally, Q-Markers were further validated through radar chart modeling, Monte Carlo simulations, and chemometric analyses. Results: Through a comparison of the machine learning models, XGBoost outperformed other models, exhibiting high and stable performance with NDCG, MAP, and Recall values ranging from 0.84 to 0.95. For the first time, the XYHJ prescription was comprehensively evaluated across its chemical profile, DMPK properties, quantitative content, manufacturing traceability, and biological efficacy. Using the optimal XGBoost ranking model, 15 components were screened and ranked, successfully identifying paeoniflorin, albiflorin, and glycyrrhizic acid as critical Q-Marker. The reliability of the ranking approach was further validated by integrating a previously published radar chart model with Monte Carlo simulations with over 10 000 sampling iterations. Furthermore, fingerprint similarity and chemometric analysis demonstrated the effectiveness of these Q-Markers in distinguishing XYHJ produced through different manufacturing processes. Conclusion: This study developed a machine learning-driven ranking framework that unifies multiple Q-Marker discovery strategies. Using XYHJ as a case study, this approach not only enhances its quality control system but also provides a valuable reference for the standardization and modernization of other TCM prescriptions.

title: Ginsenosides and their biomaterials in arthritis treatment: Challenges and strategies for advancing therapeutic potential of Chinese herbal medicines
abstract: Arthritis is an inflammatory and immune response in joint involving bone and cartilage that causes bone damage and degeneration, eventually leading to irreversible bone destruction, such as joint deformity. Current clinical treatments primarily focus on anti-inflammatory strategies and regulation of immune tolerance. However, these treatments are often associated with side effects, including infections and immunosuppression, while no existing therapy can fully address these issues. Ginsenosides, as bioactive components in traditional Chinese herbal medicines, can effectively treat arthritis through their anti-inflammatory effects, regulation of metabolism and immunity, and promotion of bone protection and repair. Moreover, the development of interdisciplinary medicine and engineering has facilitated the creation of biomaterials loaded with ginsenosides, which is conducive to improving the bioavailability of ginsenosides and promoting bone formation for the repair of bone damage. This review explores the pharmacological mechanisms of ginsenosides in arthritis treatment and evaluates the current status and limitations of their clinical application. It further discusses combination pathway, mechanism of action, therapeutic advantages and limitations of biomaterials loaded with ginsenosides for arthritis treatment in current stage of basic research. The review aims to summarize the theoretical foundations of ginsenosides in treating various types of arthritis and provide strategies and perspectives for achieving and optimizing their clinical transformation.

title: Potential of Rehmanniae Radix for treatment of diabetes mellitus
abstract: Rehmanniae Radix (RR, Dihuang in Chinese), the tuberous root of Rehmannia glutinosa , has long been used a medicinal herb in traditional Chinese medicine. It has attracted growing interest for RR’s potential effects in diabetes mellitus (DM), a chronic metabolic disorder characterized by persistent hyperglycemia resulting from insulin deficiency and/or insulin resistance. Many pharmacological studies have shown that RR and its bioactive components (iridoid glycosides and RR polysaccharides) were able to reduce blood glucose levels and DM complications. A classical formula, Liuwei Dihuang Pill, containing prepared RR, has been widely used as an adjunctive therapy for glycemic control and the prevention or mitigation of DM complications. However, processing substantially alters the chemical profile of prepared RR compared to dry RR. This review systematically summarizes current evidence regarding the therapeutic potential of RR and its bioactive constituents in type 1 and type 2 DM models. In addition, this study discusses the compositional changes of RR active components after processing and evaluates the potential and safety risks of prepared RR for the treatment of DM.

title: Integrated network pharmacology and metabolomics to reveal therapeutic mechanism of Qingxin Formula against doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity through Nrf2/HO-1/NQO1 axis to suppress ferroptosis
Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic risk in polycystic ovary syndrome: a risk-oriented perspective from integrated Chinese-Western medicine
abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), recently proposed to be renamed polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), is a common reproductive endocrine disorder in women of reproductive age with substantial metabolic heterogeneity and important long-term cardiovascular and kidney implications. Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome provides a stage-based framework for understanding the progression from dysfunctional adiposity and metabolic risk clustering to subclinical target-organ injury and overt cardiovascular and kidney disease. This review summarizes the epidemiological, clinical, and mechanistic evidence linking PCOS with the CKM continuum. Women with PCOS frequently exhibit obesity, insulin resistance (IR), type 2 diabetes mellitus, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, dyslipidemia, hypertension, and metabolic syndrome, which may contribute to progression from CKM stages 1-2 toward stages 3-4. PCOS is also associated with subclinical cardiovascular abnormalities, cardiovascular events, glomerular hyperfiltration, tubular injury, and increased kidney risk, with additional vulnerability during pregnancy, the postpartum period, and the menopausal transition. Mechanistically, IR, adipose tissue dysfunction, and hyperandrogenemia constitute major upstream abnormalities, while chronic low-grade inflammation and oxidative stress contribute to downstream tissue injury; gut microbiota dysbiosis and epigenetic remodeling may further modify this process. Based on these findings, we propose the “cardio-renal-metabolic-ovarian axis” as an integrative, hypothesis-generating framework linking ovarian endocrine dysfunction, systemic metabolic amplification, and cardio-renal target-organ injury. We further propose CKM stages 2-3 as a potential window for PCOS-specific integrated Chinese-Western prevention, combining lifestyle intervention, metabolic risk control, early cardio-renal screening, evidence-based pharmacotherapy, and adjunctive traditional Chinese medicine (TCM). Prospective studies are needed to validate PCOS-specific CKM risk stratification and determine whether earlier intervention improves long-term cardiovascular and kidney outcomes.

title: Curcumin in non-small cell lung cancer: Orchestrating tumor suppression through epigenetics
abstract: Lung cancer is the leading cause of cancer-related mortality globally. Among these, current therapies for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) are facing limitations due to toxicity, drug resistance, and inadequate efficacy. Curcumin, a natural polyphenolic compound, demonstrates significant anti-NSCLC potential through epigenetic regulation and cellular biological interventions. Epigenetically, curcumin modulates DNA methylation, histone modification and non-coding RNA networks; cellularly, it inhibits proliferation, induces apoptosis, and blocks invasion-metastasis cascades. This review examines curcumin’s mechanisms in NSCLC therapy, emphasizing its epigenetic reprogramming and multidimensional biological effects. These insights provide novel perspectives for natural product-based drug development for the treatment of NSCLC.

title: Efficacy and safety of Zaoren Ningxin Dripping Pills for treatment of insomnia (heart-liver blood deficiency syndrome): A multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase III clinical trial
abstract: Objective Given that current pharmacotherapy for insomnia often fails to improve daytime dysfunction and raises safety concerns, this study aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of Zaoren Ningxin Dripping Pills (ZNDP), a modern traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) preparation derived from Suanzaoren Decoction, in patients with insomnia associated with heart-liver blood deficiency (HLBD) syndrome. Methods This multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase III clinical trial was conducted in China. Adult patients who met the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders, Fifth Edition (DSM-5) criteria for insomnia and the TCM syndrome differentiation criteria for HLBD were enrolled. Participants were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive ZNDP (7.5 g per bag, one bag nightly) or a matching placebo for 28 consecutive days. The primary efficacy endpoint was the change in total Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) scores from baseline to day 29. Other endpoints included changes in Insomnia Severity Index (ISI) scores, sleep diary parameters, TCM syndrome scores, and Benzodiazepine Withdrawal Symptom Questionnaire (BWSQ) scores, as well as safety. Results A total of 456 participants were enrolled. By day 29, the reduction in total PSQI score from baseline was significantly greater in the ZNDP group than in the placebo group (least-squares mean difference, −0.79; 95% CI, −1.27 to − 0.31; P = 0.001). The proportions of participants achieving relative PSQI score reductions of ≥ 30% and ≥ 50% from baseline were all significantly higher in the ZNDP group than in the placebo group ( P < 0.01). At day 29, participants treated with ZNDP also showed significantly greater improvements than those receiving placebo in total ISI scores, ISI daytime function subscores, sleep latency, sleep duration, wake time after sleep onset, and the number of nocturnal awakenings recorded in sleep diaries. Additionally, significant improvements were also observed in total TCM syndrome scores ( P < 0.05). The overall incidence of adverse drug reactions (ADRs) occurred in 10.6% of participants in the ZNDP group and 15.1% in the placebo group. No ADRs leading to treatment discontinuation or study withdrawal occurred in the ZNDP group. Two weeks after treatment completion, no significant between-group difference was found in the changes in BWSQ scores ( P = 0.458). Conclusions ZNDP significantly ameliorated sleep quality, insomnia severity, daytime functioning, and TCM syndrome scores in patients with insomnia associated with HLBD. These findings suggest that ZNDP is an effective and well-tolerated therapeutic option for this patient population.

title: Multi-omics dissection of species-specific divergence and root-endophytic fungal-metabolite associations in two endangered Pleione medicinal plants
From blanket protection to targeted strategies: Insights into conservation of rare and endangered medicinal plants
abstract: With ecological, economic and cultural values, rare and endangered medicinal plants (REMPs) remain an important focus of global biodiversity conservation. However, broad-based conservation approaches may not adequately address their specific, potentially leading to mismatches between conservation efforts and outcomes. The conservation of REMPs extends beyond species protection per se, encompassing multiple objectives, including maintaining medicinal quality, safeguarding traditional knowledge, and ensuring sustainable resource use. Accordingly, it is essential to incorporate the distinctive resource attributes of medicinal plants into existing conservation frameworks, identify key conservation needs, refine conservation strategies, and establish conservation priorities. Reliable baseline information on medicinal plant diversity, distribution, and conservation status is essential for effective conservation planning. On this basis, developing a collaborative governance mechanism that integrates top-down decision-making with bottom-up feedback may help improve the targeting and effectiveness of conservation interventions.

title: Bioactive components and mechanisms of sea buckthorn in the prevention and treatment of hepatic diseases
abstract: Sea buckthorn (SB, Hippophae rhamnoides L.) is a traditional Chinese medicine with a long history, and its berries have been widely used in the food and medical industries. SB contains various types of bioactive metabolites, including flavonoids, polysaccharides, carotenoids, and terpenoids. In vivo and in vitro pharmacological studies have demonstrated that SB extracts and components are beneficial for treating liver diseases, such as liver injury, alcoholic liver disease, metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease, liver fibrosis and liver cancer. The hepatoprotective mechanisms of SB primarily include anti-oxidant, anti-inflammatory, reduction in liver fat accumulation, regulation of the intestinal microecology and inhibition of liver cells apoptosis. The Nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2, nuclear factor- κ B, AMP-activated protein kinase and peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor mediated signaling pathways are the key targets through which SB produces multiple mechanisms of liver protection. This review summarizes the pharmacological evidence of the effects of extracts and bioactive components of SB on liver diseases and reveals the limitations of the current research, which provide scientific clues for the development of liver-protecting agents from SB.

title: Characteristic coumarins with anti-neuroinflammatory potential from Wikstroemia lungtzeensis
abstract: Objective Wikstroemia lungtzeensis (Thymelaeaceae family) is a plant species whose genus includes several members used in traditional medicine for the treatment of traumatic injuries and other ailments. This study was conducted to systematically investigate the chemical constituents of the whole plant of W. lungtzeensis and evaluate their potential anti-neuroinflammatory activities. The research aims to address the limited knowledge of this plant’s phytochemistry and medicinal value, thereby exploring the genus Wikstroemia as a source of bioactive natural products. Methods The chemical constituents were isolated from the whole plant of W. lungtzeensis using modern chromatographic separation techniques. Structural identification was performed through comprehensive analysis of spectroscopic data, supplemented with advanced chemistry development (ACD) and electronic circular dichroism (ECD) calculations. The anti-neuroinflammatory effects of all compounds were assessed using a lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced BV-2, an immortalized murine (C57BL/6-derived, RRID: CVCL_0182) microglial cell line model. Results Phytochemical investigation led to the isolation and identification of twelve coumarins, including four previously undescribed compounds, named lungtzeensises A–D ( 3 , 4 , 10 , and 11 ), along with eight known analogues ( 1 , 2 , 5–9 , and 12 ). In the bioactivity evaluation, six coumarins ( 1 , 2 , 4 , 5 , 7 , and 8 ) exhibited significant inhibitory effects on neuroinflammation, with half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC 50 ) values ranging from 4.76 to 89.02 μmol/L. Notably, compound 5 demonstrated the most potent activity (IC 50 = 4.76 μmol/L), which was approximately 14-fold stronger than the positive control, minocycline (IC 50 = 67.08 μmol/L). Conclusion The findings confirm that W. lungtzeensis is a rich source of diverse coumarins, several of which possess significant anti-neuroinflammatory properties. The exceptional potency of compound 5 highlights its potential as a promising lead compound for further development. This study provides a solid scientific foundation for the medicinal utilization of W. lungtzeensis and contributes to the search for novel anti-neuroinflammatory agents from natural resources

title: Phytohormone regulation of specialized metabolism in woody medicinal plants: Mechanisms and prospects
abstract: Woody medicinal plants are invaluable sources of specialized metabolites, such as terpenoids and flavonoids, with wide applications in pharmaceuticals and cosmetics. However, the sustainable utilization of these metabolites is constrained by long growth cycles, limited productivity, and pronounced yield instability under environmental stresses. This review summarizes current advances in understanding how endogenous phytohormones—particularly jasmonic acid, ethylene, abscisic acid, and salicylic acid—coordinate the biosynthesis of these valuable compounds. We detail phytohormone-mediated transcriptional regulatory networks involving Myelocytomatosis transcription factors (MYC), APETALA2/ethylene-responsive factors (AP2/ERF), WRKY transcription factors (WRKY), and MYB transcription factors (MYB), which orchestrate the activation of key biosynthetic genes in response to developmental and stress signals. Furthermore, we critically evaluate the limitations of exogenous elicitors applications and discuss the potential of manipulating endogenous phytohormone pathways for precision regulation. Finally, we highlight knowledge gaps in phytohormone crosstalk and propose future research directions, including precision elicitation, molecular breeding, and metabolic engineering, to achieve sustainable and efficient enhancement of specialized metabolite production in woody medicinal plants

title: Jichuanjian ameliorates slow transit constipation through modulation of epithelial–mesenchymal transition associated with Wnt signaling
abstract: Objective Slow transit constipation (STC) is a gastrointestinal disorder that significantly affects patients’ quality of life. Epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) may contribute to epithelial dysfunction and reduced mucus secretion, leading to intestinal dysmotility and STC. Jichuanjian (JCJ), a traditional Chinese medicine formula, is widely used for STC treatment, but its mechanism remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the efficacy of JCJ alleviating STC and its mechanism. Methods A loperamide-induced STC mouse model was used to evaluate JCJ effects by detecting defecation time, fecal weight and water content, intestinal propulsion rate, and histopathological changes. Prediction of JCJ components distributed in serum and colon combined with RNA-sequencing (RNA-seq) showed JCJ relieved STC by regulating epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) via the Wingless-related integration site (Wnt) signaling pathway. Alcian Blue-Periodic Acid-Schiff staining (AB-PAS staining), immunohistochemistry, Masson staining, immunofluorescence and quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR) were applied to assess EMT markers, colonic mucus secretion, collagen deposition, intestinal injury, and Wnt pathway key genes. Results JCJ dose-dependently increased fecal water content, shortened the first black stool defecation time and elevated intestinal propulsion rate in STC mice; JCJ-H with the best efficacy was chosen for subsequent mechanistic assays. JCJ modulated EMT through the Wnt signaling pathway to restore intestinal motility and defecation. It downregulated EMT markers collagen type I alpha 1 ( COL1A1 ), collagen type Ⅲ alpha 1 ( COL3A1 ), fibronectin 1 ( FN1 ), N-cadherin ( CDH2 ), Snail family transcriptional repressor 2 ( SNAI2 ), zinc finger E-box-binding homeobox 1 ( ZEB1 ), upregulated tight junction proteins (Claudin-1, Occludin), promoted goblet cell mucus secretion, and increased colonic aquaporin-3 ( AQP3 ) and aquaporin-9 ( AQP9 ). JCJ also normalized the dysregulated Wnt-related genes glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor ( Glp1r ), secreted frizzled-related protein 4 ( Sfrp4 ), mucin 1 ( Muc1 ), Trefoil factor 2 ( Tff2 ), estrogen receptor 2 ( Esr2 ) in STC mice. Conclusion These results demonstrate that JCJ alleviates STC by regulating intestinal EMT through the Wnt signaling pathway, improving intestinal motility and defecation. The findings provide a mechanistic basis for targeting intestinal EMT in STC treatment and support the clinical application of JCJ as a therapeutic strategy for STC.

title: Identification of a key glycosyltransferase and de novo biosynthesis of rare oleanane-type pseudoginsenoside RT1 in Saccharomyces cerevisiae
abstract: Objective Pseudoginsenoside RT1 (RT1) is a rare oleanane-type ginsenoside from Panax japonicus with promising pharmacological potential, but its application is restricted by low natural abundance and inefficient extraction. This study aimed to identify the glycosylation steps associated with RT1 biosynthesis and to establish an engineered yeast strain for its de novo production. Methods Candidate uridine diphosphate glycosyltransferase ( UGT ) genes were screened by co-expression analysis using PjbAS1 and PjbAS2 as bait genes and further prioritized by phylogenetic analysis. PjUGT67 was cloned from P. japonicus and functionally characterized in Escherichia coli . Its enzymatic properties, substrate specificity, donor preference, and subcellular localization were investigated. To reconstruct RT1 biosynthesis, the relevant pathway genes were stepwise introduced into Saccharomyces cerevisiae , together with a heterologous uridine diphosphate xylose (UDP-Xyl) supply module, followed by strain optimization and stability evaluation. Results Pj UGT67 was identified as a UGT capable of catalyzing the conversion of chikusetsusaponin IVa (IVa) to RT1. The enzyme showed optimal activity at 35 ℃ and pH 7.0, was predominantly localized in the cytoplasm, displayed narrow acceptor specificity, and utilized both UDP-Xyl and uridine diphosphate glucose (UDP-Glc) as glycosyl donors. In addition, Pj CSLM and Pj C28UGT were verified to catalyze the conversion of oleanolic acid (OA) to calenduloside E (CE) and CE to IVa, respectively, thereby defining the sequential glycosylation route from OA to RT1. By integrating OA biosynthesis, sequential glycosylation, and UDP-Xyl supply in yeast, an engineered strain RT1-02 was constructed and achieved de novo RT1 production at 17.34 mg/L. Serial passaging further confirmed the genetic and production stability of the engineered strain. Conclusion This study provides biochemical evidence for the previously unresolved xylosylation step of RT1, identifies and characterizes Pj UGT67 as a functional UDP-xylosyltransferase involved in the terminal glycosylation step, and establishes a yeast-based route for de novo RT1 production. These findings provide new enzymatic resources and a useful basis for the sustainable biosynthesis and future engineering of OA-type ginsenosides.

title: Biocultural refugia as landscape anchors for sustainable utilization of rare and endangered Chinese medicinal materials: A perspective
abstract: Rare and endangered Chinese medicinal materials face a crisis beyond species loss—the erosion of landscapes and cultural systems that sustain them. Drawing on our spatial phylogenetics research identifying biocultural refugia in the Hengduan Mountains, southeastern Tibet, and Hainan, China, where phylogenetic diversity of ethnomedicine plants co-occurs with intact traditional knowledge, and stewardship studies revealing how local ecological knowledge (LEK) sustains phylogenetically clustered medicinal resources, we propose a “landscape anchor” framework for sustainable utilization. This framework comprises four layers: core habitat protection, traditional stewardship buffer zones, sustainable harvesting and imitative habitat cultivation areas, and technology innovation interfaces. Integrating spatial phylogenetics, LEK, and landscape governance, it offers a biocultural complement to technological approaches, with equitable benefit-sharing connecting to breeding, chemical characterization, biosynthesis, and biomanufacturing themes.

title: Identification of chemical components and metabolic prototype components in Mahuang Decoction and pharmacokinetic study of main components in normal group and ALI model rats
abstract: Objective Existing pharmacokinetic studies on Mahuang Decoction (MHD) are restricted to healthy rats, and the material basis underlying its therapeutic efficacy against acute lung injury (ALI) remains poorly elucidated. This study aimed to characterize the chemical composition of MHD and its prototype components in rat plasma, urine and feces using liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry, and further compare the pharmacokinetic characteristics of MHD’s major active constituents between normal and ALI model rats. Methods In this study, MHD was prepared according to the requirements of the Key Information Table of Ancient Classical Prescriptions, and ultra performance liquid chromatography-quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry (UPLC-Q-TOF-MS) technology was used. The chemical components of MHD and the prototype components in rat plasma, urine and feces after oral administration of MHD were identified via comparisons of reference materials, secondary fragment checks and the fragmentation patterns of different compounds in the literature. On the basis of the main active components detected, a UPLC-MS/MS quantitative analysis method for MHD was established. The differences in the pharmacokinetics of the main components of MHD were analyzed after oral administration in normal rats and ALI rats. Results A total of 109 chemical components were identified from MHD. A total of 72 prototype components were identified from plasma, urine and feces samples of rats after oral administration of MHD, including 49 in plasma, 53 in urine and 41 in feces. The systemic exposure of palmitic acid, pseudoephedrine, amygdalin, liquiritigenin and methylephedrine was significantly increased in ALI rats. The absorption of cinnamaldehyde and p- hydroxybenzoic acid decreased markedly. Conclusions In this study, we analyzed the chemical composition of MHD, detected its prototype components in rat plasma, urine and feces, and clarified its in–vivo pharmacokinetic profiles in acute lung injury. This work provides a solid basis for subsequent pharmacological investigations of MHD.

title: A systematic multi-omics-based investigation into distinct tissues of Cinnamomum cassia
abstract: Objective This study systematically investigated the chemical constituents, spatial distribution of bioactive components, and medicinal properties of seven Cinnamomum cassia tissues (root, xylem, bark, twig, leaf, petiole, and fruit), as well as the metabolic regulation mechanisms underlying the opposite drug effects of bark and fruit in kidney- yang deficiency syndrome (KYDS) rats, aiming to provide a scientific basis for the comprehensive utilization of this resource. Methods Untargeted metabolomics was employed to identify volatile and non-volatile constituents. Spatial distribution of bioactive components was mapped by atmospheric pressure matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry imaging (AP-MALDI-MSI). To mitigate the volatility of cinnamaldehyde and methoxycinnamaldehyde during imaging, a derivatization method using the Girard’s reagent T (GiRT) was developed. Medicinal properties were evaluated in rats with KYDS through assessments of hypothalamic–pituitary–target gland axis function, hepatic energy metabolism, and thermotropism. Untargeted serum metabolomics was conducted to elucidate the metabolic mechanisms underlying the opposing medicinal properties of bark and fruit. Results Untargeted metabolomics combined with AP-MALDI-MSI revealed pronounced variations in both the chemical composition and spatial distribution of metabolites across the seven tissues. The GiRT-based derivatization strategy enabled effective spatial visualization of volatile constituents, including cinnamaldehyde and methoxycinnamaldehyde. Pharmacological assessment of the restorative effects on hypothalamic–pituitary–target gland axis function and hepatic energy metabolism in KYDS rats demonstrated that twig, leaf, and petiole exhibited “Hot” properties comparable to bark, whereas root, xylem, and fruit displayed “Cold” properties analogous to those of Coptis chinensis , a classical “Cold” medicine. Notably, thermotropism analysis in KYDS rats identified fruit as the most representative “Cold” tissue among the seven tissues. These opposing “Hot” (bark) and “Cold” (fruit) properties are likely attributable to their distinct phytochemical profiles. Serum metabolomics subsequently revealed the divergent endogenous metabolic perturbations induced by these two tissues, and integration of these complementary datasets further elucidated the metabolic regulatory mechanisms and the intricate exogenous–endogenous metabolite–metabolic pathway interactions underlying their opposing properties. Conclusion This study represents the systematic multi-omics-based investigation into the distinct tissues of C. cassia , thereby enhancing the holistic understanding and utilization of C. cassia resources.

title: Characterization of a dihydrocaffeic acid-coenzyme A ligase and three dihydrocaffeoyl acyltransferases catalyzing formation of kukoamine A in Lycium barbarum
abstract: Objective Lycii Cortex (Digupi in Chinese) (root bark of Lycium barbarum ), a widely used traditional Chinese medicine, accumulates bioactive phenolamides named kukoamines. The enzymes catalyzing kukoamine formation in L. barbarum remain unknown. This study aims to characterize the key coenzyme A (CoA) ligase and BAHD acyltransferase (a plant-specific acyltransferase family) that catalyze formation of kukoamine A. Methods Candidate genes were identified using BLAST and phylogenetic analysis. Catalytic functions and substrate specificities were characterized through recombinant protein expression, in vitro enzymatic assays, and chromatographic and mass spectrometric analyses. Molecular modeling and site-directed mutagenesis were performed to identify key residues involved in catalysis. Results Three BAHD acyltransferases (BAHD-ATs), L. barbarum acyltransferase 1/6/7 (LbAT1/6/7), along with a dihydrocaffeic acid - coenzyme A ligase, L. barbarum CoA ligase 1 (Lb4CL1), were identified. LbAT1/6/7 represent the first functionally characterized dihydrocaffeoyl-CoA: spermine acyltransferases that catalyze kukoamine A biosynthesis. Phylogenetic analysis revealed that they showed distinct phylogenetic divergence from most characterized polyamine BAHD-ATs. Further mining of the One Thousand Plant Transcriptomes Project (1KP) database identified a lineage-specific expansion of these polyamine BAHD-AT genes within the Solanaceae family. LbAT6 exhibited broad substrate promiscuity, accepting multiple polyamine substrates and diverse hydroxycinnamoyl-CoA derivatives as acyl donors. Structural modeling and site-directed mutagenesis identified critical residues governing the catalytic activities of LbAT6 and Lb4CL1. Conclusion This study identified Lb4CL1 and LbAT1/6/7 as the key enzymes catalyzing the formation of kukoamine A, and laid a foundation for the production of kukoamine A as well as its derivatives.

title: Structural characteristics and anti-neuroinflammatory activity of a pectin-like polysaccharide from Ferula sinkiangensis
abstract: Objective Ferula sinkiangensis is a rare and endangered traditional medicinal material. However, its non-resin parts are often neglected, leading to a waste of resources. This study aims to isolate and characterize a polysaccharide from the roots of F. sinkiangensis and evaluate its anti-neuroinflammatory activity, thereby exploring the potential value of plant’s non-resin parts. Methods A polysaccharide, FSP70-3–1, was obtained from F. sinkiangensis roots through water extraction, alcohol precipitation, and chromatography separates. Structural elucidation was accomplished through multi-technique analyses. The anti-neuroinflammatory activity was assessed in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced BV2 microglia (immortalized murine microglial cell line) by measuring cell viability, nitric oxide (NO) production, and inflammatory gene expression. Results FSP70-3–1 is a homogeneous polysaccharide [weight-average molecular weight (Mw) = 6.34 × 10 4 ), mainly composed of D -mannose ( D -Man), L -rhamnose ( L -Rha), D -galacturonic acid ( D -GalA), D -glucose ( D -Glc), D -galactose ( D -Gal), and L -arabinose ( L -Ara). Its backbone consists of → 2,4)- α - L -Rha p -(1 → 4)- α - D -GalA p -(1→, and FSP70-3–1 can significantly inhibit the production of NO and down-regulate the mRNA expression levels of cyclooxygenase-2 ( Cox2 ), inducible nitric oxide synthase ( Nos2 ), interleukin-6 ( Il6 ), tumor necrosis factor- α ( Tnfα ) , and interleukin-1 β ( Il1β ) in LPS-induced BV2 microglia cells. Conclusion FSP70-3–1 was isolated from the roots of F. sinkiangensis and structurally characterized. It significantly reduced LPS-induced neuroinflammation in BV2 microglial cells. These findings highlight the neuroprotective potential of FSP70-3–1 and contribute to the utilization of this endangered plant.

title: Nano-potassium silicate reshapes the phyllosphere microbiome and maintains yield of Fritillaria cirrhosa
abstract: Objective Potassium limitation constrains the productivity of Fritillaria cirrhosa in alpine ecosystems. Silicate-based nano-potassium materials offer enhanced foliar absorption and improved nutrient-use efficiency. However, the effects and underlying mechanisms of nano-potassium silicate (NKSi) fertilization on F. cirrhosa yield and the phyllosphere microbiome remain unclear. Methods Field experiments with different potassium sources and application rates were conducted to evaluate their effects on F. cirrhosa bulb yield and alkaloid profiles. 16S rRNA gene and ITS amplicon sequencing was performed to characterize phyllosphere bacterial and fungal communities. Community composition, diversity, co-occurrence network, and correlation analyses were conducted to explore microbial responses to fertilization and their associations with alkaloid profiles and yield. Results NKSi (4 g/m 2 ) achieved yields comparable to those of potassium sulfate (K) fertilizer (38 g/m 2 ), whereas potassium silicate (KSi) fertilizer resulted in significantly lower yields compared to both the K and NKSi treatments. In terms of quality, KSi significantly reduced the relative contents of peimisine and peiminine compared to K, whereas NKSi was comparable to K. NKSi substantially altered the composition of bacterial and fungal communities, enriched dominant genera such as Pseudomonas, and simultaneously reduced bacterial diversity. The keystone Pseudomonas taxa were the most enriched under NKSi and were positively associated with yield. Network analysis further indicated that NKSi resulted in the most complex bacterial co-occurrence network, characterized by greater connectivity and centralization, while simultaneously simplifying cross-domain co-occurrence correlations between bacteria and fungi. Conclusion Overall, NKSi represents a promising low-input fertilization option for the sustainable cultivation of this endangered alpine medicinal plant.

title: Optimized phosphorus management enhances steroidal alkaloid biosynthesis in Fritillaria cirrhosa via rhizosphere microbiome modulation
abstract: Fritillaria cirrhosa is an endangered medicinal plant valued for its steroid alkaloids. Phosphorus (P) has been shown to enhance alkaloid biosynthesis in plants, making P management essential for conserving these valuable resources. However, optimal P rate and its regulatory mechanisms for F. cirrhosa alkaloid accumulation remain unclear. This study conducted a field experiment with six P application levels (P0–P5) to investigate their effects on alkaloid accumulation. The results showed that the P4 treatment (36 g/m²) enhanced the levels of peiminine and sipeimine by 25.5% and 24.5%, respectively, in comparison to the P0. This optimal P rate also significantly enhanced the activity of soil enzymes, including alkaline phosphatase, β-glucosidase, and peroxidase (p < 0.05). Furthermore, P addition prompted a structural reorganization of the microbial community. Co-occurrence network analysis revealed that the P4 treatment increased the complexity and connectivity of both bacterial and fungal communities. Crucially, the relative abundance of putative pathogenic fungi was minimized under P4 (23.4%), while beneficial bacterial taxa (e.g., Pseudomonadaceae, Enterobacteriaceae) and fungal taxa (e.g., Diversispora, Quaeritorhiza haematococci) were enriched. These beneficial microbes showed positive correlations with alkaloid levels (r > 0.6, p < 0.05). Structural equation modeling further validated that appropriate P application modulates the rhizosphere microbiome and potentiates soil enzyme activities, ultimately culminating in improved quality of F. cirrhosa. This study offers theoretical insights and management strategies aimed at improving the productivity and quality of F. cirrhosa, as well as other endangered alkaloid-producing medicinal plants.

title: Future of rare and endangered medicinal material substitutions: key strategies, challenges, and prospects
abstract: Owing to the combined impacts of anthropogenic and natural factors, rare and endangered traditional medicinal materials are experiencing progressive depletion, thereby necessitating urgent acceleration of research into viable substitutes. This article comprehensively reviews policies and strategies governing the development of substitutes for rare and endangered traditional medicinal materials, with particular emphasis on critically evaluating the respective advantages and limitations of natural versus artificial replacement strategies. Traditional medicinal materials originate from biological processes and consist of complex compounds accumulated by cells through intricate metabolic activities. These components form an interconnected organic whole within traditional medicinal materials. Their therapeutic efficacy typically arises not from isolated compounds but from the synergistic interactions among multiple components upon administration. Therefore, a “homologous substitution” strategy is proposed: using cells derived from original medicinal materials and employing biotechnologies such as stem cell culture and organoid cultivation to produce substitutes for traditional medicinal materials. The characteristics of this strategy can be summarized as “same origin, same quality, same efficacy”. Additionally, this study introduces a strategy to accelerate biomimetic mineralization for obtaining structurally specific mineral medicinal materials. Overall, this study aims to advance research and development of substitutes to alleviate the growing restrictions on the use of rare and endangered traditional medicinal materials.
